public_rationale: The located 89% figure concerns an earlier analysis of selected top startups, not a verified current total for all AI startups. Loss reporting also uses differing measures. Searches did not produce a readable, reconciled seven-year commitment schedule or evidence quantifying the majority-financing dependency. These are assertions about existing financial conditions and agreements, so the seven-year wording does not make the claim a forecast awaiting 2033.
limitations: Several relevant primary disclosures could not be read and were not cited as evidence.
Unknown accounting bases prevent a definitive money verdict.
The opinion about whether demand makes sense is outside the factual assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Demand for AI services has never made sense: Anthropic and OpenAI make up 89% of all AI startup revenues, both are unprofitable, and they have agreed to spend over $1.3 trillion in the next seven years, most of which depends on continued funding and debt.

statement.excerpt: Demand for AI services has never, ever made sense, with Anthropic and OpenAI making up 89% of all AI startup revenues and both of them being both unprofitable and agreeing to spend over $1.3 trillion in the next seven years, most of which is contingent on continual funding and debt.

from_speaker: most of which is contingent on continual funding and debt
our_interpretation: The assertion that demand never made sense is opinion; assess the accompanying financial propositions.
Read revenues as realized revenue, not annualized run rate.
Use July–September 2026 for the ongoing revenue-share and profitability assertions, as the latest ordinarily reportable quarter before publication.
Assess agreements already in place at publication, with spending due over the following seven years through November 17, 2033.
Read most as more than half of the commitment amount and distinguish economic financing dependence from an express contractual funding condition.
The metric_scope records the spending-commitment component; revenue concentration and profitability require separate metrics.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable current revenue totals establish the 89% share, both companies have net losses on the stated basis, and non-overlapping agreements exceed $1.3 trillion within seven years with more than half demonstrably dependent on additional financing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched records materially refute the revenue share, either company's net-loss status, the amount and timing of commitments, or the majority-financing dependency.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic and OpenAI now capture 89 percent of revenue among top AI startups, according to an analysis by The Information.
evidence.explanation: The article describes a group of 34 top startups. This earlier selected-group estimate does not establish 89% of all startups' realized revenue in the current target period.

evidence.excerpt: The WSJ, citing internal documents, reported an adjusted operating loss excluding stock-based compensation of about $10.9 billion.
evidence.explanation: Shows why the available OpenAI loss reporting cannot simply be substituted for a matched net-income comparison of both companies. This is a secondary account, not the underlying internal financial record.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A period-matched startup revenue dataset, comparable financial statements, and a deduplicated schedule of binding commitments and their financing requirements through November 17, 2033.
